data.content_ref: inline:The target addresses the comparison side of the question but never identifies what evidence within a single evaluation would distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer — the explicit distinguishing evidentiary criterion the problem requires. Its counterconditions only flag literacy/author-competence failures; they do not supply the requested diagnostic (e.g., performance on altered cases where checklist compliance would mislead, or item-level alignment of reasoning steps with correct outcomes rather than mere end-answer agreement). The CPU/checklist framing explains how reliability could arise but does not answer how, in one evaluation, one would tell apart 'the panel reliably tracks truth' from 'the panel reliably follows the checklist and the checklist happens to be right.'
